data.title: Phosphorylation of the translational repressor PHAS-I by the mammalian target of rapamycin
data.authors: Brunn GJ; Abraham RT et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: mTOR directly phosphorylates 4E-BP1 (PHAS-I), releasing eIF4E and establishing mTOR's role in translational control.
data.abstract_excerpt: The immunosuppressant rapamycin interferes with G1-phase progression in lymphoid and other cell types by inhibiting the function of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR). mTOR was determined to be a terminal kinase in a signaling pathway that couples mitogenic stimulation to the phosphorylation of the eukaryotic initiation factor (eIF)-4E-binding protein, PHAS-I. The rapamycin-sensitive protein kinase activity of mTOR was required for phosphorylation of PHAS-I in insulin-stimulated human embryonic kidney cells.

extracted_findings.effect: mTOR is a terminal kinase phosphorylating the translational repressor PHAS-I (4E-BP1)
